item.title: Neil Young Sues Donald Trump Committee For $10 Million Over Rally Song
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Neil Young sued Donald Trump 47 Committee Inc. for $10 million, alleging his song played at an Ohio rally without permission.
item.content:encoded:
Neil Young sued a Trump political committee for $10 million after he said “Rockin’ in the Free World” played at another rally without his permission. The singer-songwriter filed his copyright lawsuit against Trump 47 Committee Inc. on Monday, October 26, in Virginia federal court, according to Courthouse News Service.

His complaint pointed to the song playing before President Donald Trump took the stage at an October 12 midterm campaign event in Youngstown, Ohio. The committee faced the claim, while Trump was not named as an individual defendant, Rolling Stone reported.

Young also said the dispute carried a cost beyond the use of a recording: he claimed the association hurt his reputation by suggesting he backed Trump, according to TheWrap. His lawyers argued that the message of the song, with its focus on people left behind, conflicted with the politics of the president using it.

“In short, the song is the opposite of everything that Donald J. Trump stands for,” the filing stated, as quoted by TheWrap.

Young had already taken the Trump campaign to court in 2020 over “Rockin’ in the Free World” and “Devil’s Sidewalk.” That case ended in December 2020 after a settlement that included a promise not to use the song without permission, TheWrap reported.

The new lawsuit alleged the committee lacked the license it needed and had used the song at other events aimed at winning Republican votes in the midterms, Courthouse News Service reported.

The fight over the song stretched back to Trump’s 2015 presidential campaign announcement, when Young publicly objected to its use. He objected again in 2018, Rolling Stone reported, years before the settlement now cited in his latest case.

A separate fight over campaign music reached court in 2024, when the family of R&B great Isaac Hayes challenged Trump’s use of “Hold On, I’m Coming.” Isaac Hayes III announced that a judge had granted an injunction preventing its use at campaign rallies, as AllHipHop reported at the time.

Young’s lawsuit also asked the court to bar the committee from playing any of his songs. Rolling Stone said the White House, the committee and the Republican National Committee did not immediately answer its requests for comment.

item.title: Boosie Badazz Set To Perform With Full Orchestra In Little Rock
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Boosie Badazz brings "The Black Tie Experience" to Little Rock on January 2, with The Signature Orchestra backing his catalog.
item.content:encoded:
Boosie Badazz is taking “The Black Tie Experience” to Little Rock, Arkansas, with a January 2, 2027, date booked at Robinson Center.

The Saturday night show will pair his Southern Hip-Hop catalog with The Signature Orchestra, giving fans a chance to hear his music backed by a live ensemble. The production draws on a recording career that spans more than two decades.

“The Black Tie Experience was created to give audiences a different way to experience Boosie live,” a Stage View Presents spokesperson said in an announcement published by SWARK Today.

Robinson Center’s performance hall seats 2,222. The venue dates to 1939 and underwent a $70 million renovation, according to its website.

For the Little Rock concert, doors are scheduled to open at 7 p.m., an hour before the 8 p.m. show.

The ticket seller limits purchases to nine tickets per person and per credit card. Ticketmaster lists October 23, 2026, as the start of the general sale.

The spokesperson said the production’s size makes touring difficult and limits the number of cities it can reach. Bringing it to Little Rock, the organizer said, would give fans across Arkansas and nearby areas access to the show in a theater setting.

That booking honored Boosie’s Bad Azz and Webbie’s Savage Life, putting the two rappers and those albums at the center of the production. For Dallas, the venue billed a set built around orchestral arrangements of the rappers’ existing work, placing live musicians behind their familiar records.

Another Southern rapper has been taking his catalog into that setting, too. Jeezy announced a second Las Vegas residency, “The Legend Of The Snowman,” an orchestral, black-tie production.

His run at PH Live at Planet Hollywood is set for May and June 2026. While his previous residency focused on Let’s Get It: Thug Motivation 101, the second centered on his broader brand and legacy.

item.title: Nolan Wells March Brings Oxford Students Out For Answers
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Nolan Wells' family sought answers as students marched in Oxford and held solidarity events at Rider and Mississippi State.
item.content:encoded:
Nolan Wells‘ name was back on signs at the University of Mississippi on October 25 as students and Oxford residents marched for answers about his death.

University of Mississippi freshmen Christopher Burnett and Avah Trevino organized the event, The Daily Mississippian reported. They walked from Fulton Chapel past the Walk of Champions, the Circle and James Meredith’s statue before returning.

“We just want, simply, for the family’s questions to be answered in further investigation,” Burnett said.

The demand had also reached Rider University, where its NAACP college chapter held an October 22 walk, according to The Rider News.

President E’miija Eccles brought campus Black organizations into the event and contacted Public Safety three weeks ahead. Participants made at least three laps around Centennial Lake.

Founding chapter president Naa’san S.J. Carr, a 2024 graduate, returned to speak. “We gather because remembrance matters, but so does the pursuit of truth and repair,” Carr said.

The marches followed the September 22 Jackson County grand jury decision to bring no criminal charges. Jurors found insufficient evidence to accuse anyone of a crime in the death of the 18-year-old, who had gone to Horn Island with friends for July 4.

Jackson County District Attorney Angel Myers McIlrath said there was no evidence that Wells’ death was racially motivated. Through defense attorney Edward Paltzik, Warren Hudson, Jax Pitalo and Morgan Seymour maintained their innocence.

The state autopsy left the cause and manner of his death undetermined, while grand jurors described the circumstances as consistent with drowning.

The Wells family hired civil rights attorney Ben Crump and sought a second autopsy, separate from the state’s examination.

Relatives have said they still want answers about what happened during Wells’ last hours on the island.

At Mississippi State, students rallied on the Drill Field on October 16, The Reflector reported. The Mississippi chapter of the Party for Socialism and Liberation organized it.

NAACP political action co-chair Dave Claggette helped lead the event. Speakers urged students to vote and stay politically involved.

After about an hour, participants held a moment of silence for Wells and Richard E. Holmes, MSU’s first Black student.

item.title: Loe Shimmy Adds Brent Faiyaz To Halloween “Zombieland” Concert
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Loe Shimmy added Brent Faiyaz to his Halloween concert with BigXthaPlug, Sexyy Red and Rob49 at Miramar Amphitheater.
item.content:encoded:
Loe Shimmy is bringing Brent Faiyaz into his Halloween plans, adding the singer to the lineup for his “Zombieland” concert in South Florida.

Faiyaz joins BigXthaPlug, Sexyy Red and Rob49 for the October 31 show at Miramar Regional Park Amphitheater in Miramar, Florida. The concert starts at 8 P.M. Saturday, giving Shimmy a close-to-home stage to bring his rap and R&B collaborators together.

The costumes could pay off, too. A $5,000 cash prize is at stake in the night’s costume contest. The night also includes a haunted house, and Shimmy’s team says the Halloween attractions will include a zombie invasion.

A bigger plan is behind the party.

The venue describes “Zombieland” as the start of Shimmy’s push to build an annual Halloween event. It cites Tyler, The Creator’s Camp Flog Gnaw and Travis Scott’s Astroworld as inspirations for that goal.

The concert’s name also runs through Shimmy’s catalog.

He released Zombieland 2 in March 2024 and expanded it with Zombieland 2.6 that June. The Halloween show turns that recurring theme into a night of music and haunted attractions.

Faiyaz has already been part of Shimmy’s music for years. The pair released “For Me (Remix)” in November 2024, with the track also appearing on Nardy World.

Their partnership continued on “Run The World,” from Shimmy’s Pretty Girlz Run The World. Sexyy Red is on that album as well, joining him on “5 Star Freak.”

For Shimmy, the South Florida show follows the North American tour behind Pretty Girlz Run The World. His team says he recently finished that run, bringing the Halloween date back to the region where he built his name.

AllHipHop was covering the Pompano Beach rapper when he released “Fallin” in 2022. That coverage noted his work with Kodak Black and an early Drake co-sign. Now he’s putting several of his collaborators on the same event bill.

Tickets are available through Ticketmaster. The listing says all ages are welcome and the event will take place rain or shine. Ticket sales are final and nonrefundable.

item.title: French Montana & D-Block Europe’s Copenhagen Concert Is Canceled Too
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: French Montana and D-Block Europe's November 4 Copenhagen concert was canceled, with ticket buyers awaiting more information.
item.content:encoded:
French Montana and D-Block Europe canceled their November 4 show in Copenhagen. The Danish stop joins the other dates fans will miss on their European run.

The rappers were booked to play Store VEGA on Wednesday, November 4. VEGA’s event page now carries a cancellation notice. The venue says ticket buyers will receive more information from the ticket provider. It gives no reason for the cancellation.

The notice does not lay out a refund process for buyers. The page lists a price of 495 Danish kroner, including fees.

Ticketmaster also marks the Copenhagen event as canceled under its listing for the “Worldwide Wave Tour.” The bill paired the British duo with French, the Moroccan-American rapper. They had already made music together.

French appeared on “If I Was Rich Enough” from D-Block Europe’s PTSD 2. They also teamed up on “Fully Loaded,” a collaboration VEGA highlighted when promoting the concert. The planned night paired the duo’s melodic UK rap with French’s American catalog, bringing their studio connection to a shared live bill.

Copenhagen joins two other canceled joint dates AllHipHop previously reported: October 30 at AFAS Live in Amsterdam and November 6 at Raiffeisen Halle im Gasometer in Vienna.

AFAS Live attributed its Amsterdam cancellation to “unforeseen circumstances” and said Ticketmaster would email ticket holders.

VEGA’s notice does not give that explanation for Copenhagen. Ticketmaster’s Vienna listing also labels that concert canceled without explaining why.

D-Block Europe consists of Young Adz and Dirtbike LB. Their third studio album, Rolling Stone, reached No. 1 on the UK’s Official Albums Chart in January 2024, according to Official Charts.

The record-breaking album brought together guests Kodak Black, Yxng Bane and Noizy.

London remains listed separately. Ticketmaster still offers a ticket link for D-Block Europe’s October 28 date at The O2 and includes French Montana in the lineup. For Copenhagen ticket buyers, VEGA directs the next update to the ticket provider.

item.title: Yella Beezy Trial: MO3’s Girlfriend Testifies
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Yella Beezy's trial heard from MO3's girlfriend as his defense challenged the cash evidence behind the murder-for-hire case.
item.content:encoded:
Yella Beezy faced testimony from MO3’s girlfriend Tuesday (October 27) as his lawyers challenged the cash trail behind the state’s murder-for-hire case.

The Dallas rapper, legally named Markies Conway, pleaded not guilty to capital murder. He denied paying Kewon White to kill MO3 and faced life in prison if convicted. MO3’s legal name was Melvin Noble.

Jocylynn Jackson told jurors she suspected her address had reached others after MO3 was killed shortly after leaving her apartment, according to FOX 4.

She said Devin Brown, her children’s father and a co-defendant, had asked their son whether MO3 was there. Brown denied involvement in a message shown in court.

Phone records presented to jurors showed Brown repeatedly calling the boy that morning. Jackson said she had been subpoenaed and did not want to testify.

Defense lawyer Toby Shook argued the bills Yella Beezy withdrew differed from cash recovered from convicted gunman White. He also accused investigators of overlooking Brown’s personal dispute with MO3.

The testimony followed Monday’s jury selection in Dallas, where Judge Chika Anyiam questioned 75 potential jurors about whether news coverage would affect their judgment. The case reached that stage after a monthlong delay.

White’s separate trial ended with a September 4 conviction and a life sentence. He shot MO3 with a rifle after chasing him on foot along Interstate 35E in Dallas on November 11, 2020.

The state’s case against Yella Beezy had already drawn a dispute over rap lyrics. Prosecutors said the music helped establish why the killing happened and what he intended. His lawyers argued the songs told creative stories rather than documented actual events.

Another witness agreement involved Jose Bodega, Yella Beezy’s childhood friend. The rapper, whose legal name is Theodore Thomas, agreed to cooperate in the murder case through a deal in a separate federal drug prosecution.

Their music connection included Bodega’s appearance on the song “Tool On Ya” with Yella Beezy and Trapboy Freddy.

At an October 6 hearing, defense expert Julianna Moore described Bodega’s guilty plea to drug conspiracy and his agreement to help prosecutors. She also testified that prosecutors dismissed a gun charge against him, a point the defense could challenge when examining his testimony.

item.title: Drake’s “Janice STFU” Accuser Withdraws Copyright Lawsuit
item.dc:creator: Nolan Strong
item.description: Drake's "Janice STFU" copyright lawsuit was withdrawn by songwriter GoodbyeCalev after the rapper's team denied his claims.
item.content:encoded:
Drake saw the copyright lawsuit over “Janice STFU” withdrawn less than two weeks after a songwriter accused him of copying its chorus.

Rolling Stone reported that Aviel Calev Hirschfield voluntarily dismissed the lawsuit barely 10 days after filing it. The publication cited a recent court filing.

The Portland producer, known professionally as GoodbyeCalev, had sued Drake on October 16 in California federal court. The complaint also named OVO Sound LLC, UMG Recordings Inc. and Universal Music Publishing Inc.

Drake’s team had denied the claims and called the lawsuit “manufactured and baseless.” His representatives maintained that he wrote the song himself.

GoodbyeCalev’s complaint described a chorus he said he developed with Drake in mind over music from production duo FnZ. He alleged that he completed his demo around January 25, 2026, sent it to producers who worked with Drake and heard nothing back.

“Janice STFU’s chorus is literally identical to the Copyrighted Work in lyrics, melody, and cadence,” the complaint alleged.

The dispute involved more than what listeners heard. GoodbyeCalev alleged that his manager gave Drake’s representatives separate recording files and their metadata to support his account. He also alleged that Drake’s lawyers demanded he stop publicly claiming authorship.

A recording presented as his demo later circulated on X. A legal representative for GoodbyeCalev told Pitchfork that the leaked audio matched the recording submitted as evidence in the case. The producer’s claim rested on his account of when that recording was made.

The song’s musical roots were already public. “Janice STFU,” from Iceman, interpolated Lykke Li’s 2011 song “I Follow Rivers”. Drake had used Li’s music years earlier too, sampling “Little Bit” on his 2009 mixtape So Far Gone.

GoodbyeCalev and Drake also shared writing credits on Beyoncé’s “Heated,” from Renaissance. In a 2023 Willamette Week interview, GoodbyeCalev described how his manager circulated a track that Beyoncé picked up. He said the money from “Heated” helped him buy gear for his Southwest Portland studio after years working as a rapper, producer and engineer.

His now-withdrawn complaint sought damages and profits tied to the alleged infringement, along with a jury trial. It did not put a dollar figure on his claimed losses.

item.title: EXCLUSIVE: Lil Durk Offers Up Music Income To Get Out Of Jail, Lul Pab’s Mom Doesn’t Object
item.dc:creator: Grouchy Greg Watkins (@GrouchyGreg)
item.description: Lil Durk offered future music earnings as bond security after his acquittal, with Sony and major artists backing his release bid.
item.content:encoded:
Lil Durk put his future music income on the line in a new bond push, offering earnings he could lose if he fled.

His lawyers filed the proposal asking Judge Michael W. Fitzgerald to reconsider keeping the Chicago rapper behind bars after his recent acquittal.

The filing offered future royalties, publishing income, money tied to his name and image, touring earnings and cash and property from supporters.

“In support of his release, we offer a bond package so robust that should Mr. Banks violate his release conditions, both he and his family would be left destitute indefinitely,” his lawyers wrote.

Drew Findling, Marissa Goldberg, Brian Steel and Christy O’Connor submitted the brief, which said that while prosecutors opposed release, the slain man’s family did not.

In an attached September 28 letter, Andrea Robinson, mother of Saviay’a “Lul Pab” Robinson, left that decision to the judge considering the rapper’s request.

“On behalf of the family of Saviay’a Robinson, we do not object to Durk Banks being granted a bond if it is deemed appropriate by the Honorable Court,” she wrote.

The federal case grew out of an August 19, 2022 shooting near Los Angeles’ Beverly Center that killed Pab. Prosecutors alleged the intended target was his cousin, rapper Quando Rondo, whose legal name is Tyquian Bowman.

They accused Durk of financing a murder-for-hire plot that sent gunmen after Quando Rondo in Los Angeles. The government claimed the attack was retaliation for the November 2020 killing of King Von during a confrontation involving an associate of Quando Rondo.

Authorities took Durk into custody in October 2024, and he denied the accusations. On September 11, 2026, a jury acquitted him on five murder-for-hire and stalking counts heard in the first trial.

The verdict left him in custody because he also faces separate murder-in-aid-of-racketeering and firearms charges that remained pending, with another trial still ahead. He pleaded not guilty and now wants to be released.

“Following eleven days of evidence and argument and three days of deliberation, the jury unanimously found that Mr. Banks did not beyond a reasonable doubt participate in the conspiracy to stalk Mr. Bowman that ended in Mr. Robinson’s death,” the lawyers wrote.

They also argued that the verdict weakened the court’s earlier concerns about flight and possible interference with witnesses who testified against him.

“The jury’s full acquittal of Mr. Banks sends a clear message about his chances of success at a second trial, and diminishes the likelihood that he would violate his bond conditions should he be released,” the defense wrote.

His lawyers cited an earlier ruling to explain why the new offer went beyond the cash and property already proposed as security.

“[Lil Durk] would still have his intellectual property with which to earn a handsome living abroad. Any set of conditions would need to impoverish [Lil Durk] and lead to the forfeiture of all interest in his intellectual property,” Judge Fitzgerald wrote in the earlier order.

So, the new offer covers digital radio royalties plus publishing rights from Durk’s albums Almost Healed and Deep Thoughts, according to his lawyers.

It also included merchandise, branding and other income tied to his name, image and likeness. Touring completed the four streams, though lawyers acknowledged he could not tour while on the run.

“Mr. Banks offers to encumber each of these future income streams,” his lawyers wrote. “Of course, this encumbrance on his intellectual property is in addition to the other significant collateral: the home that Mr. Banks’ mother lives in, and a significant sum of cash and property proffered by friends who have placed their trust in Mr. Banks.”

Sony Music Entertainment backed part of the proposal in a September 14 letter signed by executive Stephanie Yu and included with the court papers.

“This letter will serve as confirmation that Sony Music Entertainment is prepared to guarantee an appearance bond for Mr. Banks up to an amount of $1,000,000,” Yu wrote.

“Separately, we have also agreed that Mr. Banks is allowed to forfeit his future earnings toward the bond in an amount to be determined by this Honorable Court.”

Letters from JAY-Z, J. Cole, Michael Rubin and former Cook County State’s Attorney Kim Foxx also supported the request or described Durk’s character and community work.

The defense said therapy, sobriety and his Muslim faith had changed his life before his arrest. The filing said he completed a 30-day inpatient drug treatment program with encouragement from his wife, India.

JAY-Z’s letter described Durk helping young artists from his community secure recording contracts, giving them work in music and a route beyond limited neighborhood opportunities.

Cole explained that Durk insisted on the hopeful message behind their collaboration “All My Life,” even after Cole asked him for a different song.

“He wanted to push a message of change and of peace and of growth and maturity, and he thought that if I got on this song with him it would have the greatest impact,” J. Cole wrote.

item.title: Romeo Miller Joins Hulu’s “The Mob”
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Romeo Miller joined Hulu's "The Mob," a celebrity competition with Parker Posey and up to $250,000 in cash prizes at stake.
item.content:encoded:
Romeo Miller joined Hulu’s “The Mob,” putting the rapper in a villa with 11 other celebrities with up to $250,000 in cash prizes at stake.

The reality competition premiered Monday, October 26. Parker Posey hosts and also serves as an executive producer.

According to Hulu, the group picks a don who controls who gets paid, stays or leaves. The others can overthrow that leader. Each episode brings jobs drawn from mob movies, with the cast competing in an Italian villa.

Some of Miller’s castmates have played their own parts in crime families on screen.

Aida Turturro played Tony Soprano’s sister Janice on “The Sopranos.” Debi Mazar’s credits include “Goodfellas,” “Entourage,” and “Younger.” Their acting careers put them alongside reality stars from dating shows and Bravo.

Joe Gorga, of “The Real Housewives of New Jersey,” is Melissa Gorga’s husband and Teresa Giudice’s brother.

Harry Jowsey has appeared on “Too Hot to Handle,” “Dancing With the Stars,” and “Let’s Marry Harry.” Maria Georgas entered “The Bachelor” during Season 28, when Joey Graziadei was the lead, before joining this cast. Willam Belli competed on Season 4 of “RuPaul’s Drag Race” and also works as an actor and recording artist.

Miller already had years of TV work behind him before this cast came together. As Lil Romeo, he built a rap career and had his own Nickelodeon series, “Romeo!,” which ran from 2003 to 2006.

The son of Master P later appeared on “Growing Up Hip Hop”, alongside Angela Simmons, Rev. Run’s daughter, and Boogie Dash, Damon Dash’s son. By July 2017, Miller was among the returning cast members as that series entered its third season.

The show followed the children of music stars as they told their own stories.

U.S. viewers can watch on Hulu, including through Hulu on Disney+ with a bundle subscription. Outside the United States, the series is available on Disney+.

item.title: Megan Thee Stallion Explains How Silence Over Her Contract Led To Regret & Legal War
item.dc:creator: Mike Winslow
item.description: Megan Thee Stallion revisited her early contract fears as her music business moved toward ownership and creative control.
item.content:encoded:
Megan Thee Stallion said she once feared questioning her record deal. She spoke at Overcoming Impossible Live at 1 Hotel Brooklyn Bridge in New York City.

Entrepreneur and Robert Irvine organized the event for business owners. The program paired small-group work with afternoon talks from Megan, Gary Vaynerchuk and Irvine.

“I was a little bit nervous about asking questions,” she told Entrepreneur.

What followed were years of fights over her music.

As AllHipHop previously reported, Megan signed with Carl Crawford’s 1501 Certified Entertainment in 2018 and sued the label in 2020. In October 2023, the two sides settled and parted ways. They kept the terms private.

During that dispute, Megan accused 1501 of blocking releases and keeping her under contract after she had fulfilled its terms. She also sought outside oversight of the label’s finances to ensure it could pay a potential judgment. Crawford disputed that request and accused her of using it to harass the label.

“I started realizing I’m not making as much money as I should be making because I kind of just gave my life away to somebody else,” Megan Thee Stallion said. “I had to take a step back and think, Okay, let me see what’s going on with my contracts. Let me figure out how I can be my own boss.”

Her next deals put ownership at the center. In February 2024, Warner Music Group announced an agreement that left Megan with her masters and publishing.

Releases would come through her own Hot Girl Productions, with Warner providing distribution and help with radio and marketing. She also kept creative control. She could bring artists signed to her imprint into Warner’s network if she chose.

She had already started releasing music through her own company before the Warner deal.

“Cobra” arrived in November 2023. In its announcement, Warner counted “HISS” as the second solo song she released through her company.

A more recent deal continued that approach.

On August 14, 2026, Megan announced a distribution partnership with Interscope Records. The announcement said Hot Girl Productions would remain home for her releases, and she would keep her masters and publishing while receiving global distribution and strategic support.

“I’ve always wanted to create music on my terms while building a legacy that extends beyond the industry,” Megan said in that announcement.
